en: A THREE-DAY STEP (14 Sep 2026). This is the first scan since 11 Sep - the 12 and 13 Sep runs did not happen - so every comparison in this file is against 11 Sep, and all windows moved three days at once.
Read directly from Chrome: GSC, GA4, the Ahrefs web UI, Brand Radar, and a full same-origin crawl of all 108 pages. No OpenSEO, no Supermetrics, no Ahrefs API.

THE BIG WIN - SITE-WIDE SPEED RECOVERY. All 108 crawled pages now respond in under one second. Site mean TTFB 959 -> 571 ms, median 895 -> 533 ms, slowest page 2,286 -> 843 ms. The homepage went 1,571 -> 741 ms on crawl and 1,442 -> 480 ms on navigation. This fully reverses the TTFB regression that dropped the audit health score on 11 Sep.

THE SECOND WIN - GOOGLE'S SITEMAP READ CAUGHT UP. Last read moved 3 Sep -> 13 Sep and Discovered pages 99 -> 109, now matching the origin exactly. The sitemap staleness flagged since 7 Sep is cleared.

GSC fell, and the window explains most of it. The 28-day window slid three days to 15 Aug-11 Sep: clicks 48 -> 46, impressions 1,468 -> 1,333 (summed across all 28 DAYS rows), position 30.3 -> 30.8, queries 107 -> 98. CTR rose 3.3% -> 3.5% only because impressions fell faster than clicks.

THE ADELAIDE PAGE-ONE CLUSTER IS GONE. On 11 Sep six Adelaide rendering queries sat on page one; today only two Adelaide queries appear at all, at positions 38.0 and 42.0. All 17 remaining page-one queries are brand terms. Not one non-brand commercial query reaches page one.
Brand still carries search: dxliving 22 + dx living 17 = 39 of 46 clicks (84.8%). Every non-brand query in the 98-row table is still at zero clicks, as it has been for the life of this series.

THREE NEW ARTICLES, the first since 7 Sep: plan-vs-actual-reporting-construction, 3d-rendering-for-architects-australia and construction-programme-visualisation. Sitemap 106 -> 109 URLs, 82 -> 85 articles. All three are hub-linked immediately and return 200 with one H1, a canonical and a meta description.
But the three new articles ship WITHOUT FAQPage schema, which 66 of the existing 85 articles carry. That is a regression in the publishing template and the cheapest fix on this list.

GA4 rose with the window: 595 sessions (up 24), 3,042 events, 347 users; Direct 212, Organic Search 192, Organic Social 180, AI Assistant 9. Organic Search carries 5 of the 7 key events at 65.63% engagement.

ZERO KEY EVENTS ACROSS BOTH 7-DAY WINDOWS for a NINTH consecutive scan (7-13 Sep and 31 Aug-6 Sep). All 7 key events in the 28-day window predate 31 Aug. Tagging is healthy - GTM, Ads and GA4 IDs all load and dataLayer is populated - so this is a conversion problem, not a measurement one.
Organic Social delivers 180 sessions, 30% of the site, at 4 SECONDS average engagement time and zero key events. Facebook alone is 164 sessions across four source rows, more than google / organic.

Ahrefs authority grew but the shape did not: referring domains 329 -> 338 and backlinks 354 -> 368; all-time 514 and 568. DR and UR still 0 because 88.5% of domains and 88.9% of backlinks are nofollow. Crawled pages 176 = 159 + 2 + 15 + 0 + 0, with 404s flat at 15 for a tenth reading.

AI visibility flat at 30/100 for an eighth scan: 21 AI responses and 10 cited pages, unchanged (ChatGPT 12/5, Copilot 8/6, Perplexity 1/1). With three new articles and no new citations the citation surface actually thinned, 12.2% -> 11.8%. Brand Radar still tracks 0 prompts on a twentieth reading.

THE /ARTICLES OVERLAY IS ON DAY EIGHTEEN. A full-viewport white fixed div at z-index 99999 still covers the hub, and the viewport centre resolves to BODY. Crawlers see all 85 articles; humans see a blank white page. Twenty articles are reachable only from that hub.
GSC has still NOT rebuilt Page indexing - the build is dated 4 Sep for an eighth reading, so 87 indexed / 119 not indexed is ten-day-old data and should not be read as current.
Not re-measured today and recorded as null rather than guessed: third-party corpus, AI share of voice, and Core Web Vitals (Chrome UX Report still has insufficient data for both device types).
